value: Machinery and related products in the categories listed in Annex I, Part A
rows.text: Under Art. 6(1) and Art. 25(2), Annex I, Part A categories must use EU type-examination (module B) with module C, full quality assurance (module H), or unit verification (module G). Annex VII, 4 and Art. 33(2) show these procedures involve a notified body. Annex I, Part B categories may use internal production control (module A, Art. 25(3)(a)), so they need a notified body only when harmonised standards or common specifications are not applied.

value: EU type-examination (module B, Annex VII) followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C, Annex VIII)
Conformity based on full quality assurance (module H, Annex IX)
Conformity based on unit verification (module G, Annex X)
rows.text: Under Article 25(2) of the Regulation, for machinery in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer (or the person referred to in Article 18) applies one of three procedures: module B plus C, module H, or module G. Article 6(1) confirms that Part A machinery is subject to these procedures.

rows.value: Annex I, Part A, point 5 (the category of machinery and related products subject to third-party conformity assessment)
rows.text: A safety component with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches that ensures safety functions falls under Annex I, Part A, point 5. Recital 54 explains that such components are included in Annex I and must undergo third-party conformity assessment, whether or not they are placed independently on the market.

Under Annex III point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation (and Annex I point 1.3.8.1 of the Directive), guards for moving transmission parts are either fixed guards or interlocking movable guards. Interlocking movable guards are to be used where frequent access is envisaged. The Regulation words this as 'shall be used'; the Directive says 'should be used'.
The passages do not include requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III. They only cover 1.3.3 and 1.5.13, plus headings and general parts, so its risks cannot be determined from them.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is considered the manufacturer and takes on the manufacturer's obligations under Article 10. A non-professional user modifying their own machinery for their own use is not.
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation, whoever carries out a substantial modification of machinery is treated as its manufacturer and is subject to the Article 10 obligations. If the modification affects only part of an assembly of machinery, those obligations apply to the affected machinery. That person must declare conformity on their sole responsibility and apply the conformity assessment procedure in Article 25(2), (3) and (4). A non-professional user who modifies their own machinery for their own use is excluded.

value: EC declaration of conformity (EU declaration of conformity under the Regulation)
Instructions for use and the related information
rows.text: Under Directive Art. 5(1)(e), the EC declaration of conformity must accompany the machinery, and Art. 5(1)(c) requires the necessary information, such as instructions, to be provided. Under the Regulation, Art. 15(2)(b)-(c) says distributors must check that the machinery comes with the EU declaration of conformity and the instructions for use and information (in an easily understood language). Under Art. 10(5), identification details (model, year of construction, serial number) may also go in an accompanying document if they cannot be put on the machinery itself.

Under Art. 10(3) of the Machinery Regulation, the manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product is placed on the market or put into service. Other product directives and regulations in the passages also set 10 years.

Under Article 54, the Regulation applies from 14 January 2027, except for certain provisions that apply earlier (e.g. Articles 26 to 42 from 14 January 2024; Article 50(1) from 14 October 2023; Article 6(7), 48 and 52 from 13 July 2023; Article 6(2)–(6), (8), (11), 47 and 53(3) from 14 July 2024).

Under Art. 52(1) of the Regulation, only products placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 14 January 2027 are protected from being impeded. Machinery first placed on the market on 16 January 2027 is not covered by that transitional provision.

rows.value: INAIL, within 45 days of the employer's request
rows.text: Under art. 71, c. 11 of D.Lgs. 81/2008, the employer uses INAIL for the first periodic verification of Annex VII equipment, and INAIL must carry it out within 45 days of the request. If that period passes without action, the employer may choose another qualified public or private body. Art. 2, c. 1 of DM 11 April 2011 gives 60 days instead. I have followed the 45 days in the legislative decree, which is the higher-ranking source and the one stated in its current wording.

rows.value: For a suitable period of time (no fixed number of years is given)
rows.text: Under Art. 5(3) of Directive 2009/104, the employer must record the results of work-equipment inspections, keep them at the disposal of the authorities, and keep them for 'a suitable period of time'. The passages set no specific duration. The Italian rule (art. 71, c. 11) only says the reports must be kept and made available to the supervisory body.

The passages do not answer this. They contain no catalogue of models and no rule or date (such as 20 January 2027) that moves products from internal checks to notified-body assessment. They only cover notified-body procedures and 10-year record-keeping under several directives and regulations.

The passages do not identify model RC-5 or its characteristics, and they give no rule tied to 20 January 2027. Recitals 20 and 54 of the Regulation only describe general principles, so no specific conformity assessment procedure for RC-5 can be determined.

The passages do not say whether model CS-400 may stay with internal production control after 20 January 2027. None of them covers conformity assessment procedures, the use of internal production control, or the CS-400 model. They also give no transitional rule that sets 20 January 2027 as a relevant date.

The passages do not answer this. None of them gives the contents of Annex I, Part A of the Regulation or of Annex IV of Directive 2006/42/EC. The only related material is a correlation table for Directive 98/37/EC, and the Annex IV and Annex I passages shown contain no category lists.

Vehicle servicing lifts are listed in Annex I, Part A, point 3. The internal production control (module A) route for products built to harmonised standards is in Art. 25(3), which covers only products listed in Annex I, Part B. Art. 25(4) allows module A only for categories not listed in Annex I at all. On these passages, module A alone is therefore not available for such a lift. The passages give no dates, so they do not address the 20 January 2027 cut-off, and they do not say which procedure Part A products must use.

Article 20(9) refers to the essential health and safety requirements in Annex III, sections 1.1.9 and 1.2.1, 'as regards protection against corruption and safety and reliability of control systems'. None of the passages compares the Regulation with Directive 2006/42/EC, so they do not say which requirement is new.

The passages do not give a correspondence for Article 12 of Directive 2006/42/EC. The only Regulation correlation table provided (Annex X of Regulation 2016/425) concerns Directive 89/686/EEC, not Directive 2006/42/EC.
The passages contain no correlation table for Directive 2006/42/EC, so they do not say which Regulation annex corresponds to its Annex IV.

Position 8 is an overhead travelling crane in Table A2 of the IGEA sheet, and point 2.3 says verification follows the intervals in Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08. The passages do not give the DEMAG crane's capacity, type, sector of use or year of manufacture. Allegato VII rows 12, 14 and 15 depend on those details, so the interval cannot be determined from these passages.

The passages do not give the crane's capacity or how it is used, so this assumes a load over 200 kg, not hand-operated, in regular use. On that assumption, a mobile or transferable lifting appliance built in 2017 is under 10 years old in 2026. Allegato VII row 13 then requires verification every two years (biennale). If the crane were used in a sector such as extractive work, row 12 would require annual verification instead.

The passages do not say who carries out periodic verifications after the first one on equipment listed in Annex VII. Annex VII, point 4 (EU type-examination) only describes the notified body's examination of technical documentation and specimens, and says nothing about periodic verifications.

Art. 71, c. 11 of Legislative Decree 81/2008 requires INAIL to carry out the first periodic verification within 45 days of the request. The 60 days in Art. 2, c. 1 of the 2011 Ministerial Decree conflicts with this. The passages do not state a precedence rule, so I applied the legislative decree, as the higher-ranking source.

The passages do not say whether the UR5e can be put into service on its own as delivered. They only describe assembly, mounting and first boot, and mention integration and responsibility (section 4.4) only in the table of contents. They give no statement on its legal status or on putting it into service alone.

The nanoScan3 must be thoroughly checked at least once a year (section 5.6.2, minimum requirements for the regular thorough check). This covers the principal function check and the detection capability test. Depending on the risk assessment, further checks may be needed, and daily checks of the principal function and a visual check are recommended in many cases.

Under section 4 of the IGEA technical sheet (Impegni aggiudicatario/verificatore), the verifier must plan the checks jointly with IGEA's representatives and notify IGEA at least 15 days in advance. This time is needed for the scheduling described in points 4.1–4.2.

The passages say that position 13 (IGEA-PRIM 5t overhead travelling crane, built 2017) is verified at the intervals in Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 (Scheda Tecnica points 2.3 and 2). The only Allegato VII rows provided are row 11 (construction-site lifts, annual) and row 12 (mobile or transferable lifting equipment over 200 kg, annual). Nothing shows that an overhead travelling crane falls under either row, and the row for it is not provided, so the interval cannot be determined.

The crane (position 13, IGEA-PRIM 5t, built 2017) would be over 10 years old in November 2028 (about 11 years). Under Allegato VII, riga 14, lifting equipment over 200 kg with a manufacture year more than 10 years back is verified annually, instead of the biennial check in riga 13. The passages do not say expressly that this crane is 'mobile o trasferibile' or in regular use, so this assumes both apply.

The IGEA technical sheet (point 2.3) says position 24, a piattaforma elevatrice in table A6, is verified at the intervals in Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08. The Allegato VII rows provided cover only pressure equipment and piping, not elevating platforms, so the interval cannot be determined. The passages also do not mention the HINOWA make.

The passages place position 8 in table A2 (gru a ponte scorrevole) and refer to Annex A for the last verification dates, but those dates and the Annex VII interval for overhead cranes are not provided. Overdue status on 2026-11-14 cannot be determined.
The UR10e reach is 1300 mm (ur10e-manual, section 3.1 Technical Specifications), but none of the passages states the UR5e reach, so the increase cannot be calculated.

Section 7.3 of the MA STAR manual says the load nut's wear indicator must be checked every 6 months. The pair of nuts must be replaced once the wear limit is reached, which is when the threaded pin protrudes 3 mm above the support plate.

The IGEA technical sheet (p. 5) requires the structural verification certificate of residual life cycles only for equipment more than 20 years old. The passages do not include the list entry at position 8, so the DEMAG crane's age is unknown and the question cannot be answered.
